reading.body:
NTT's Ashburn VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, about 2.2 percent of Virginia's 1,639.4 MW of disclosed data center capacity.

The facility is one of only 26 Virginia data centers that make a megawatt figure public, out of 332 mapped sites. That gap is the real finding. Published capacity in Virginia is a small, self-selected sample, and any total built from it undercounts the state's actual load. Ashburn VA7 ranks 14th of those 26, so it is a mid-sized entry in the only dataset that exists.

The 36 MW is a power number, not a compute number. At 40 kW per rack it implies roughly 900 racks, and at typical training power ratios roughly 1,100 to 1,400 accelerators, but those are conversions from an assumption, not published figures. The 125,000 square feet of technical space is the building side of the same fact. Power, floor area, and location are what this record establishes.

What it does not establish is whether the power is reserved for AI workloads or how the site connects to the grid. Those two facts decide whether a facility of this size matters to AI scaling, and neither is published. The record also carries no certifications and no announced expansion.
